newsitem.title: USA: U.S. administration seeks cost protection for BPA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. administration seeks cost protection for BPA.

text.p: The Clinton administration said Thursday that Congress should put into law mechanisms that would to protect Bonneville Power Administration's ability to recover its costs in a competitive power market.

Northwestern state governors last year completed a review of Bonneville, a federal power marketing and transmission agency that sells hydropower at cost, to see how the agency could fit into a deregulated market.

The review called for Bonneville to be split into a power marketing agency and a separate transmission agency, and recommended that utilities in the area, including Bonneville, should all hand over control of their transmission operations to an independent grid operator (IGO).
While the Clinton administration has not taken a formal position on the review, Bonneville administrator Randall Hardy said the administration was "favorably inclined" toward the recommendations.

But he said the administration was "disappointed" that the review did not adequately address how Bonneville would recover its costs, without imposing a big risk on taxpayers. The agency is carrying billions of dollars in debt.

"If the Northwest is going to seek to retain the benefits of the system, and if Bonneville's statutes are to be changed to provide more open transmission access, the position of Treasury and bondholders must be protected by assuring cost recovery," Hardy said in testimony to the House Resources Committee's subcommittee on water and power.

Fish protection measures in the Columbia River Basin dam system are one of Bonneville's biggest costs, and have helped to drive Bonneville power's rates, once the cheapest in the region, 20 percent above market.

Legislation would be needed to address how the agency can compete in the open market while it also has to meet obligations such as marketing power at cost and protecting fish and wildlife, Hardy said.
Legislation would be needed to deal with rules that give Bonneville priority access to any federal generation resources that are needed to maintain reliable grid operations.

Some of Bonneville's customers raised concern about transmission rates being developed by the Independent Grid Operator (IndeGO) for the Northwest and Rocky Mountain states, which the customers said would shift costs to BPA transmission customers.

"The (Direct Service Industries), as major BPA transmission customers, cannot support BPA joining IndeGO, if the consequence is a doubling or more of their transmission rates," Steve Waddington, executive director of the group, said in testimony to the subcommittee.
